title: Top K Frequent Elements
keyIdea: Count with a hash map, then keep a min-heap of (count, number) of size k: push each pair and pop when the size goes over k. The smallest count is always on top, so it's the one removed; the k survivors are the most frequent.

approaches.name: Brute force: count with visited
approaches.idea: For each unvisited number, count its copies with an inner loop, then sort the (count, number) pairs and take the first k.
approaches.why: The inner loop re-scans the array for every new number.

approaches.name: Hash map + sort
approaches.idea: Count with a map, put (count, number) pairs in a vector, sort descending, take the first k.
approaches.why: Counting is O(n); sorting the d distinct numbers is O(d log d).

approaches.name: Hash map + min-heap of size k
approaches.idea: Count, then push (count, num) into a min-heap and pop whenever its size exceeds k. Pop everything left into the answer.
approaches.why: The heap never holds more than k + 1 pairs, so each push/pop is O(log k).

quiz.q: Why a MIN-heap to find the MOST frequent?
options: When it overflows you drop the least frequent, which a min-heap keeps on top

quiz.q: Why push (count, num) and not (num, count)?
options: Pairs compare by their first element, so the heap orders by count

quiz.q: Can you beat O(n log k)?
options: Yes: bucket sort by count (counts are at most n) gives O(n)
